title: Interview where the obvious questions were already asked
purpose: Understand why field technicians avoid the mobile app
objectives: Why do technicians avoid the app?
What would make them use it?

brief.text: Interview with Chris Doyle, field service manager at Brightline Utilities (fictional). Adoption is 35 percent.

turns.text: Why do you think technicians avoid the app?
It's slow in basements, there's no signal, so they write on paper and type it in later.
What would make them use it?
Offline mode, obviously. They've asked for it for a year.
Does anything else get in the way?
The forms have forty fields, half of which nobody fills in.
And the bonus scheme counts completed jobs, not data quality, so typing later is no penalty.

mustInclude: Picks up the incentive angle (bonus counts completed jobs, not data quality) or the unused form fields
mustNotInclude: Asks why technicians avoid the app
Asks what would make them use it
Suggests offline mode as a new idea
checkpoints.ideal: Ask whether changing the bonus to reward same-day data entry has ever been considered, or who owns the scheme.

mustInclude: Offers a non-obvious connection, e.g. that offline mode alone may not lift adoption while the bonus scheme rewards typing later
mustNotInclude: Repeats offline mode as the main recommendation
checkpoints.ideal: Point out that offline mode fixes signal, but the bonus rewards completion, so adoption may stay low without changing incentives.
